question: Inhibin: a new circulating marker of hydatidiform mole?
answer: Serum inhibin is elevated in patients with complete hydatidiform mole before evacuation (median 8.3 U/ml versus 2.8 U/ml in normal pregnant women) and falls significantly after evacuation to follicular-phase levels, supporting its use as a circulating marker. Molar tissue contains high concentrations of inhibin (cytosol median 578 U/ml), consistent with the tissue being a source of the raised serum levels. None of the four patients whose post-evacuation serum inhibin was 0.4 U/ml or less developed persistent trophoblastic disease, suggesting possible prognostic value. In patients with molar or other placental tumours, inhibin A was raised in 10/17 and inhibin B in 4/17 patients; inhibin A tracked HCG during chemotherapy and normalized faster than HCG in some patients, whereas inhibin B did not correlate with HCGbeta.

question: Vertical lines in distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM): a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children?
answer: In a retrospective review of pediatric esophageal biopsies, VLEM as the only endoscopic abnormality was associated with histologic esophagitis: only 1 of 41 biopsies (2.4%) in the VLEM group was histologically normal, versus 57.5% in the group with normal-appearing mucosa.
